notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: By headlines of 24 November, US petrol prices have fallen 66 cents in a month, the biggest drop since 2008, gold is at its lowest this year and Israel has let flights resume, while Washington added sanctions on more than 20 entities in Iran's banking network, a former Mossad chief pressed for an attack on Iran and Qatar's emir warned the region cannot take another round. Libya says it will sue Ukraine at the International Court of Justice over the Russian warship sunk at Benghazi, Finland had the drone-hit Sparta II towed out of its economic zone, and a Russian drone spent minutes over Poland, which is receiving a NATO radar aircraft. Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang eleven days after he resigned, Trump says he made the deal, the US added Megaspeed to its commercial blacklist and Chuck Schumer wants Trump's role investigated. Kenya's governors have refused a health ministry order to stop public hospitals taking payment through their own paybill numbers, and Jordan's central bank has banned cash payment to medical providers. From 21 and 22 November stand COP31's collapse in Turkey, Anthropic's loss of 147 trillion won in market value, bitcoin's two-year low and the breaches of the FBI's crime records and the European Commission.
moved: The Iran war thread was revived on 24 November after nine editions without a narrative, and it turned: US petrol fell 66 cents in a month, Israel let flights resume and Qatar mediated, while Israeli voices pressed for a strike. New US sanctions on Iran's banking network kept an 8 November expectation; the Chronicle's 21 November reading of escalation is withdrawn.

The thread on Europe's security moved on 24 November from naming the weapon to legal and practical steps: Libya says it will sue Ukraine at the ICJ over Benghazi, Finland had Sparta II towed out of its zone, Poland is receiving a NATO radar aircraft after a Russian drone crossed, and Seoul corrected a report of a Russian airspace violation.

The Nvidia thread was resumed after five editions: Huang was reinstated with Trump claiming the deal, and the US blacklisted Megaspeed, keeping a 13 November expectation, so the costs of chips reaching China were placed on firms and hosts abroad.

A thread on health payments drawn into state channels began on 24 November. The same day two older expectations failed with nothing reported: a Likud court challenge to part of the Knesset result, and another AI or cloud company raising $10 billion or more for data centres.
silent: The thread on states underwriting data centres has had no narrative since 20 November; Trump's threatened tax on data centres built abroad came again on 24 November inside the Nvidia thread, so this looks like the editions' division more than the subject ending.

The thread on young protesters has had no narrative since 20 November, and its expectation of a German ban citing France failed on 22 November; its student protest expectations run to mid-December, so the silence may be the sample.

The thread on strikes over pay owed outside Europe has had no narrative since 19 November; on 24 November doctors in Jammu and Kashmir striking over stipends came in the new health payments thread, so part of its ground is still in the headlines.
The thread on soldiers against gangs and smugglers has had no narrative since 19 November; its Colombian and OAS expectations run to 10 and 17 December, so the silence is short.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, talks and reach
threads.text: From 26 October it followed the Gulf's talks and strike preparations and the Hormuz price shock to jet fuel, mortgages, wages and rates; the war was reported paused on 8 November, and on 11 November producers invested as if Hormuz would stay unsafe. From 13 to 21 November its events came in other threads: strikes on Bahrain and Qeshm, tankers hit off Hormuz and a US drone shot down, while four of its price expectations failed. After nine editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 24 November, by judgment, with an unlinked narrative marked plausible: US petrol fell 66 cents in a month, the most since 2008, Israel let flights resume, a former Mossad chief pressed for an attack and Qatar's emir warned against another round. New US sanctions on Iran's banking network kept an 8 November expectation. Its case against says petrol falls every autumn.
threads.direction: After strikes resumed from 13 November and reached tankers and a drone over the strait by 21 November, on 24 November the war was reported as a pause, with pump prices falling and pressure applied by sanctions while Israeli voices argue for a strike.

threads.label: Governments setting pump prices mid-war
threads.text: Begun on 7 November: Italy would not extend its diesel excise cut, Portugal adjusted its fuel tax discount and Taiwan's CPC held pump prices after absorbing NT$34.07 billion, joined as governments handing the war's fuel price back to drivers. After four editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 12 November with an unlinked narrative marked firm: Pakistan cut petrol and diesel prices, Chile resubmitted a bill freezing fuel prices until February, Greece set €32 million for islanders' sea transport and Indonesian ferry operators asked to raise fares, with crude below $90. Its case against says the decisions move in different directions and none names Hormuz. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to early December.
threads.direction: It has moved from governments ending fuel tax cuts to governments keeping pump prices in their own hands and paying the gap from budgets as crude fell below $90.

threads.label: Housing: state drives, outside money and work
threads.text: On 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing with Portugal investigating police at housing protests. On 6 November the Chronicle revived it, by judgment, when foreign buyers made 16% of Portuguese purchases as prices hit records. On 11 November it was revived again, by judgment, with a narrative marked tentative: millions of Spaniards struck over housing three weeks before a general election, a rush of withdrawals hit China's payroll housing fund, and employer-linked homes were offered in Tianhe and Taiwan. Its case against says Spain has a shortage and China a slump. On 17 November Spain's strike and Porto's housing camp came in a new thread on Europe's weekly protests, which joins them with wages and prices; the Chronicle has not revived this thread for it.
threads.direction: It has moved from states building homes, to prices set by buyers from outside, to housing argued over through strikes, payroll funds and employers.

threads.label: Shared systems failing, from outages to patches
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand, it ran through AI-led US growth, Taiwan's state buyers, borrowing and the Nvidia case to 12 November. From 12 November it followed shared systems stopping: a Microsoft outage at British councils and Australia's federal police, the FAA's nationwide halt, the fallback left to households and faults hard to tell from attacks. On 18 November South Korea's Digital Daily blamed patches for AI-found flaws for failures at the NSA, in finance and in aviation. No narrative has carried it since. Two of its early expectations failed with nothing reported: further buying by Taiwan's stabilisation fund in November, on 22 November, and another AI or cloud company raising $10 billion or more for data centres, on 24 November. Breaches of public records have had their own thread since 21 November.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and borrowing to public services stopping when one system fails, to who holds the backup, to telling a fault from an attack, and by 18 November to patches for AI-found flaws named as a cause.

threads.label: AI labs financed by suppliers, then public shareholders
threads.text: Begun on 10 November, when TSMC was reported investing NT$32 billion in OpenAI and Anthropic. Its expectation that Anthropic would cut or delay its listing failed on 17 November. On 18 November Anthropic priced at $83 a share as the ECB compared the AI build to subprime, and on 19 November it passed $3 trillion on its first day. After two editions without a narrative, while the Nasdaq's fall came in other threads, it was resumed on 22 November, marked tentative: Anthropic lost 147 trillion won of market value in one day, Kommersant tied bitcoin's two-year low to the share offering, Musk warned of an AI funding shortage next year and Oracle said it has the funds for its OpenAI contract. Its case against says the 21 November reading of high rates fits the same headlines.
threads.direction: It has moved from chip suppliers funding the AI labs, to the labs selling shares to the public at record prices, to the listing's own fall and the claim that its size draws money from other risky assets.

threads.label: Chinese makers' gains and others' answers
threads.text: Begun on 3 November: SCG's chief executive called China's cheap exports a fact of life, Thailand raised taxes on imported electric cars, and Tata Motors and Iveco formed a group. It was revived on 7 November, by judgment, when Musk said Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck and BYD's Yangwang opened pre-orders for a 2.08 million yuan car. On 8 November its own edition carried it on, with Tesla suspending orders for the Cybertruck's entry version, NIO claiming a car a minute and Yangwang launching in Abu Dhabi. On 10 November, with no narrative, The Independent reported Musk axing the Cybertruck with refunds, keeping the 7 November expectation of another US carmaker cutting an electric pickup, though by Tesla itself. No narrative has carried it since 8 November, and no headline here reports a sale lost to a Chinese maker.
threads.direction: It moved from producers elsewhere merging or taxing to meet Chinese goods, to producers elsewhere retreating, and by 8 November to Chinese makers selling abroad at both the cheap and the luxury end.

threads.label: Soldiers sent against disorder, gangs and smugglers
threads.text: Begun on 5 November, marked tentative: Indonesia's troops in Jakarta, Pakistan's army for Punjab by-elections, a Bangladeshi soldier killed raiding traffickers at Teknaf and a French bill widening when police may fire. After eleven editions without a narrative it was resumed on 19 November as crime fought as war: Haiti's forces fought gangs with Salvadoran troops in the country, Colombia's president counted a tenth bombing and weighed asking Congress for US troops, fishermen sued Washington over a drone strike at sea and the OAS called a session on organised crime. On 20 November France's parliament definitively adopted the law presuming police use of weapons lawful, keeping the 5 November expectation, in the youth protest thread. Its case against says the military role in each is decades old. No narrative carried it on 20, 21 or 22 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from soldiers keeping order on home streets to armies, aircraft and foreign troops fighting gangs and smugglers, with results counted as deaths and strikes.

threads.label: Failed banks and money cases reaching office
threads.text: Begun on 6 November. Paraguay's Congress resumed impeachment of President Santiago Peña over the Ueno bank crisis, Daniel Vorcaro's phone recorded 316 interactions with Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the Banco Master case, and UMNO's move to pay Najib Razak's RM50 million fine split Malaysia's coalition. On 8 November an unlinked narrative, placed here by the Chronicle, reported a court freezing the assets of Peña, described as former president, and his arrest over an estimated $809 million Ueno loss, with the Philippine vice-president answering wealth charges and opponents in Armenia and Egypt facing courts. No narrative has carried it since 8 November. On 12 November Sara Duterte's impeachment trial appeared in the new thread on leaders' children.
threads.direction: It moved from failed banks reaching people in office to courts reaching office-holders through money in general, with Peña going from impeachment proceedings to arrest in two days.

threads.label: Routes to work abroad rationed and deadly
threads.text: Begun on 8 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Off Lompoul in northern Senegal a pirogue capsized and at least 21 people died. In Bangladesh a lottery shortlisted 300 applicants for 112 fee-free jobs in Malaysia. A testimony in Portugal's SAPO describes shared rooms and low pay ending a migrant's stay, and in West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari promised to deport every 'Bangladeshi infiltrator'. The join is that a person's attempt to work abroad is rationed by a draw, the sea, wages or expulsion. Its case against says the lottery may be meant to cut out recruitment agents, the shipwreck's destination is not given, and four of seven headlines come from bdnews24. No narrative has carried it since 8 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Gas supply sought beside climate summit targets
threads.text: Begun on 10 November and marked tentative by its own edition. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed the last four years as the hottest on record and COP31 set out an electrification push, while Deutsche Welle examined Germany's untapped gas, Japan and Vietnam discussed an LNG project, Argentina awaited $38 billion for Vaca Muerta and Brazil extended its cooking gas programme to 2031. The join was governments securing gas while planning to electrify. No narrative has carried it since 10 November. On 22 November its expectation of a COP31 text with electrification targets but no dated fossil fuel commitment failed because no text was adopted: COP31 in Turkey ended without agreement after the EU rejected the final text, reported in a new thread on forums that need every government's consent.

threads.label: Ukraine talks and who pays in Europe
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 10 November and marked firm by its edition. US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi produced a planned prisoner exchange of 1,000 or 1,500 a side and a US offer of 'NATO-style' security guarantees with $400 million in weapons, while Merz threatened to block the next EU budget unless every member supports Ukraine and Fico called that blackmail. Its case against says Merz's demand may belong to the 2028 to 2034 budget talks. On 11 and 12 November the talks came in the seats thread, on 13 and 17 November in the strikes thread, and on 14, 19, 21 and 22 November in the thread on Europe's security. No narrative has carried the question of who pays since 10 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Pope Leo in politics, restraint on reform
threads.text: Begun on 11 November. Pope Leo XIV left Argentina after a Mass for three million, with Die Welt reporting that Javier Milei is on his own after the Pope's criticism, and arrived in Peru, where the government declared non-working days and Keiko Fujimori invited guests to meet him. In the same days the Vatican halted the reform process in the German diocese of Speyer. The join is one office speaking against a government's policy in South America while limiting lay-led reform in Germany. Its case against says popes have criticised Argentine economic policy for a decade and host governments always declare holidays for papal visits. No narrative has carried it since 11 November, so it is silent; on 21 November its Peru expectation failed, with no report of Leo XIV or the Vatican criticising a named Peruvian policy or official.

threads.label: Seats, borders and talks used as pressure
threads.text: Begun on 11 November and marked tentative: the CSTO stripped Armenia of its vote, Turkey excluded Israel from COP31 in Antalya, and Washington and Moscow asked Europe to choose one negotiator for the Ukraine talks. On 12 November it was carried on as entry of every kind: Israel will bar Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Washington's envoys said Europeans would join the next round, and Putin spoke of US visas for Russian Olympians. On 13 November the single-negotiator expectation failed when the EU agreed a team of five countries and EU institutions, which weakens the reading of entry as a bargaining move. Its ground passed on 14 November to the thread on Europe's security bargained elsewhere. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It moved from seats in alliances and summits to entry of every kind, and on 13 November Europe was admitted to the Ukraine talks on its own terms, against the thread's reading.

threads.label: Leaders' children judged on their own conduct
threads.text: Begun on 12 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice-president over a certificate scandal, Sara Duterte's impeachment trial is to resume after the ASEAN summit, Donald Trump Jr left an adviser's role at Kalshi over a conflict with a rival investment, and Nigeria's president congratulated his son Seyi on a traditional title. The join is what a leader's name entitles a child to hold. Its case against says the cases share a family tie and little else. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, but on 18 November its expectation was kept when R7 reported Brazil's prosecutor-general filing a criminal complaint against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for slandering Lula in a post about Maduro. A slander complaint fits the expectation more loosely than a resignation would.

threads.label: Nvidia scandal as a chip export enforcement dispute
threads.text: Begun on 13 November with a narrative marked firm, though the Nvidia case ran in the AI spending thread from 10 to 12 November: Bessent blamed Lutnick for Megaspeed not being blacklisted. On 17 November Nvidia reported revenue up 103%, its board refused Huang's return and Washington proposed extending chip controls to Southeast Asia. After five editions without a narrative it was resumed on 24 November, marked plausible: the board unanimously reinstated Huang eleven days after he resigned, Trump says he made the deal, shares rose from Frankfurt to Taipei and Schumer wants Trump's role investigated. The US added Megaspeed to its commercial blacklist, keeping the 13 November expectation, and Trump warned of a tax on data centres built abroad. Its case against says the decisions come from different bodies and only this reading puts them on one ledger.
threads.direction: It has moved from a dispute between US departments over who let chips reach China, to duties on transit states, to Huang's return with the president's backing while penalties fall on a distributor and on data centre hosts abroad.

threads.label: Long-range strikes during Russia and Iran talks
threads.text: Begun on 13 November, marked plausible: as the EU named its team for the Ukraine talks, a Ukrainian drone hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, bombs went off in Moscow and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain. Resumed on 17 November, marked tentative, with crossings as targets: the Crimean Bridge twice, Kyiv's bridges with 700,000 households left without power, a rail line to Hungary and Iran's Qeshm Island. On 19 November Lenta reported Trump saying Putin is angry at Zelensky over the Crimean Bridge attack, keeping the 17 November expectation. No narrative has carried it since 17 November, so it is silent; from 20 to 22 November Russian missiles in Poland and attacks on ships in the Gulf of Finland, off Hormuz and at Benghazi came in the thread on Europe's security.
threads.direction: It has moved from strikes on bases, ships and oil sites far from the fronts to strikes on bridges and islands in the days before the three-power meeting, one of which came up after it.

threads.label: Frontiers, ships and host states after the declaration
threads.text: Begun on 14 November, when Zelensky said Washington floated Ukraine giving up Donbas for NATO membership. On 19 November the Shenzhen declaration, by Observador's account, left out both wars; on 20 November Estonia set 1 December to close its Russian crossings; on 21 November drones disabled Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland; on 22 November a Russian warship was sunk at Benghazi and Polish prosecutors said Russian cruise missiles fell in Poland. On 24 November, marked plausible, the answers moved past naming the weapon: Libya says it will sue Ukraine at the International Court of Justice over Benghazi, Finland had Sparta II towed out of its economic zone, a Russian drone spent minutes over Poland, which is receiving a NATO radar aircraft, and Seoul scrambled jets then said Russia had not violated its airspace. Its case against says Benghazi is held by Moscow's allies.
threads.direction: It has moved from Europe's security bargained in a format Europe does not lead, through allies fortifying and attacks on ships, to countries where attacks land answering first by naming the weapon and by 24 November by lawsuits, tows and radar aircraft.

threads.label: Incomes set by rule falling behind prices
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. France had a fifth Saturday of protests against the cost of living and French police demanded a higher risk allowance; an Italian simulation put a 2028 pension more than 13,000 euros a year below one of twenty years earlier; a former Argentine judge warned of delays in retirees' claims, and a Canadian disability charity closed. The join is incomes fixed by law, decree or grant falling behind prices; its case against says the events share no cause. On 17 November a new thread on Europe's weekly protests took in the same French protest rounds. No narrative has carried it since 14 November, so it is silent; on 22 November pension policy through personal accounts began a thread of its own.

threads.label: Governments taking back roles in food supply
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked tentative that continues nothing. Nieuws.nl reports a fertiliser shortage caused by the Hormuz blockade threatening Dutch food security, Marib's farmers in Yemen have harvests and no open markets, Senegal calls rice a pillar of food sovereignty, New York is spending $70 million on five city-run grocery stores, Egypt's prime minister inspects a permanent state food fair, and Fortune reports nearby shops losing sales when Walmart leaves a town. The join is public authorities taking back choosing what is grown, securing inputs and selling food. Its case against says only the fertiliser story is new, Egypt's outlets date from the 1940s and New York's stores were a 2025 election promise. No narrative carried it on 17, 18 or 19 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to 5 and 12 December.

threads.label: Europe's protests over prices, met by top-ups
threads.text: Begun on 17 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts two weeks of protest over living costs and housing: 270,000 marched outside Paris on 6 November, Porto's housing camp put up tents on 8 November, Spain held its first general strike in 14 years on 11 November, and France counted 146,000 at a new round on 17 November. France brought forward a minimum wage rise and Italy's coalition argued over 300 euros for pensioners. Its case against says Spanish rents and French wages have different causes. No narrative has carried it since 17 November, so it is silent; on 20 November Gen Z marches across Europe and Bologna's general strike day came in the thread on young protesters.

threads.label: Defence decided by numbers of drones and interceptors
threads.text: Begun on 30 October with a narrative the Chronicle had not given a thread: cheap drones had made defence a matter of quantity again, so states were financing arms factories and widening conscription. After seventeen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 18 November, marked plausible, from the defending side: an Egyptian military expert told Al-Watan that closing the gap in US Patriot production will take years, the Jerusalem Post reported a rayon shortage threatening that production, Iran struck US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain and a UAE tanker, and a coalition struck the Houthis. Its case against says the Patriot shortfall has been discussed since 2023. No narrative carried it from 19 to 22 November, so it is silent; on 22 November a Polish general said a pilot ordered to shoot down a Russian missile turned back, in the thread on Europe's security.
threads.direction: It has moved from cheap drones driving arms production and conscription to interceptor stocks that factories cannot refill quickly.

threads.label: Others' trade deals while three powers meet
threads.text: Begun on 18 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing, as Trump, Xi and Putin were reported meeting in China. EU governments approved signing their trade agreement with Indonesia, Mark Carney bet on Asia-Pacific trade to reduce Canada's dependencies, Vietnam's leader called for a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, Xi asked Chile to deepen ties, Keiko Fujimori pitched Peru's Chancay port to Chinese investors and Egypt signed an industrial deal with India. The join is governments outside the meeting fixing their trade without waiting on it. Its case against says APEC leaders talk trade every November. On 19 November the meeting ended with a declaration that, by Observador's account, left out both wars, which weakens the picture of three powers bargaining over them. No narrative has carried trade since, so it is silent.

threads.label: Strikes outside Europe over pay already owed
threads.text: Begun on 19 November with a narrative marked tentative, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts strikes and protests outside Europe since 5 November in Nigeria, Egypt, Bangladesh, Canada, Chile, Mexico and South Korea: on 19 November Nigeria's lecturers demanded withheld salaries, Zamalek's players complained of late dues, Bangladeshi garment workers clashed with police and Niagara's paramedics neared a strike, while the World Bank said Bangladesh is short of revenue. The join is pay already earned or promised and not paid, often by a state short of money. Its case against says the sample leans on three Nigerian papers. No narrative has carried it since 19 November; on 24 November Kashmir doctors' strike over stipends came in the new health payments thread.

threads.label: States offering to site and underwrite data centres
threads.text: Begun on 20 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days, so the story is older than its first narrative. Trump threatened to tax or sanction US firms that build data centres abroad, Lagarde said EU funds should take first losses on chip plants and data centres, Google was reported to have cut a million TPU chips from its 2027 orders and CoreWeave fell below its listing price. The join is governments offering to locate and carry the build as private investors sell. Its case against says CNBC reported Anthropic raising $93.5 billion the same day. No narrative carried it on 21, 22 or 24 November, so it is silent; on 24 November Trump's warning of a tax on data centres abroad came again in the Nvidia thread, sending related shares down in Korea.

threads.label: Young protesters met by police and courts
threads.text: Begun on 31 October with protests called for the same weekend in several European countries, met with bans in some cities and talks in others; on 1 November its edition read them as governments meeting young protesters mainly with police numbers. After seventeen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 20 November, marked plausible and built from the site's notebook: pupils in Schleswig-Holstein struck against conscription, DW reported Gen Z protests in hundreds of European cities, keeping a 31 October expectation, a Lormont pupil went before the courts and France adopted its police weapons law. On 22 November the 1 November expectation of a German ban on a Gen Z protest citing violence in France failed, with nothing reported, as its own case against allowed. No narrative carried it on 21, 22 or 24 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from police numbers set against young protesters to courts, arrests and suspensions, and in Germany to a plan for military service.

threads.label: Breaches of records people must give the state
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked firm, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for four days, so the story is older than its first narrative. Since 18 November attackers reached Transport for London's photocard records, the European Commission's servers through an AI-assisted attack, the FBI's National Crime Information Center database and the US Agriculture Department, beside leaks of over 10 million records at Japan's DHC and 15.18 million at ZOZOTOWN and thefts from four Taiwanese banks and Binance. The join is that public bodies make up about half the list, and people cannot withdraw records the state requires. Its case against says the breaches share dates, not an attacker, the FBI case rests on one AP source, and disclosure rules shape the balance. No narrative carried it on 22 or 24 November.

threads.label: Gold, bitcoin and tech shares falling together
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. On 20 and 21 November the Nasdaq erased its gains for the year, gold fell more than $2,000 an ounce from its peak, bitcoin dropped below $55,000 for the first time since September 2024 and foreign investors pulled more than 3 trillion from Taiwan's market, as Trump attacked the Federal Reserve over rates. The join is the cost of borrowed money. On 22 November the AI financing thread read bitcoin's low instead as money drawn into AI listings; the two stand as competing readings. On 24 November gold at its lowest this year came in the revived Iran thread, read there as safe-haven buying stalling, while Al-Watan put it down to US bond yields, which is this thread's reading.

threads.label: Power projects placed on water already promised
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked tentative, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for five days, so the story is older than its first narrative. On 21 November Amit Shah backed India's Siang dam and promised dialogue with protesters, after a Sharavathi submergence report was promised to the Supreme Court on 17 November and the court refused Tamil Nadu more Cauvery water on 20 November. Taipei's mayoral campaign has fought over solar panels on the Feicui reservoir, Finland's largest conservation project failed when a utility would not sell the Palokki plant, and Bogotá warned on 18 November of water and power rationing under El Niño. The join is new hydro and solar placed on water already counted on. Its case against says half the evidence has nothing to do with power. No narrative carried it on 22 or 24 November.

threads.label: Consensus forums failing while courts and clubs decide
threads.text: Begun on 22 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. COP31 in Turkey ended without agreement after the EU rejected the final text, and UN talks on autonomous weapons ended without binding rules, while the International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya by nine votes to six and fifteen West African states adopted a migration declaration in Dakar. The join is that forums deciding by consensus failed while bodies that vote or admit only the willing reached decisions. Its case against says climate talks collapsed at Copenhagen in 2009, the ICJ's timing follows a 2019 filing, and the contrast may be between judging and legislating. No narrative carried it on 24 November, when Libya's planned suit against Ukraine at the ICJ came in the thread on Europe's security.

threads.label: Pension policy run through personal accounts
threads.text: Begun on 22 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept since 17 November, so the story is older than its first narrative. On 17 November the US Treasury set rules for automatic retirement plans and Australia debated a superannuation shake-up; on 17 and 18 November Handelsblatt explained Germany's old-age provision deposit; on 20 November Singapore topped up the CPF accounts of more than 782,000 older citizens; on 22 November the Sydney Morning Herald argued for super for workers under 18 and RNZ said KiwiSaver fails the self-employed. The join is governments acting through individual accounts rather than the public pension, which Fortune reports is under six years from a 22% US cut. Its case against says these are adjustments to systems dating from 1955 to 2022. No narrative carried it on 24 November.

threads.label: Health payments drawn into state-run channels
threads.text: Begun on 24 November with a narrative marked tentative that continues nothing. Kenya's health ministry ordered public hospitals to stop taking payment through their own paybill numbers and the governors refused; Jordan's central bank banned cash payment of dues to medical providers; Himachal Pradesh handed its new health insurance scheme to the Aditya Birla Group; and steps towards Medicare for All are on the US Democratic agenda. Public payers are slow: Rio Grande do Norte is late paying for orthopaedic surgeries, New Zealand's ACC refused a tradesman after decades of levies, and doctors in Jammu and Kashmir strike over stipends. The join is health money drawn into channels the state runs or chooses, and paid out slowly. Its case against says the motives differ, from county revenue to procurement, and the word payment may be doing the joining.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

withdrawn.held: On 30 October the Iran war's costs had turned towards easing, with Washington pressing for a lower oil price before the midterms.
withdrawn.undone: On 31 October Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64, Italy's inflation reached 5.4% and the price rise was argued over in pay rounds and tax relief in several countries. The easing reading did not last a day, and the earlier withdrawal of the outward-spread reading now looks premature.

withdrawn.held: The AI share sell-off was moving towards losses partly taken on by Taiwanese public money, through its state funds and central bank.
withdrawn.undone: On 1 November no state buying was reported, and the same thread was read as AI money landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron staff payouts and Chinese results led by AI computing. The public-money reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the thread's direction.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war thread had turned to which governments carry the fuel price and which take more of it as revenue, with US-Iran talks stuck.
withdrawn.undone: On 2 November no fuel-tax argument appeared, Brent fell 2% to $111, Trump said talks were going well and the thread was about whether a strike or talks follow the US vote. The who-pays reading rested on Turkey's single tax rise and is not carried as the direction; its expectation of a second government raising a fuel tax is still open.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on the editions since 26 October, with none stamped 28 October, 9 November, 15 and 16 November or 23 November, drawn from whichever publishers the collection reads and capped in how many headlines each may supply. Continuity between days is partly produced by the brief: today's Europe narrative carries on yesterday's by link and the Nvidia narrative resumes one from 17 November, so the writer was asked to find a thread and found one. I revived the Iran thread by my own judgment from a narrative that continues nothing, and then withdrew my 21 November reading of escalation on one edition; this thread has had more withdrawals than any other, and I may be turning with each day's headlines rather than with events. That narrative's own case against says US petrol falls every autumn and Al-Watan puts gold's fall down to bond yields, so the pause may be read into a seasonal price. In the Europe thread, Libya's suit may come from Benghazi's eastern authorities, who are allied with Moscow, and the headlines do not say which government spoke. The Nvidia narrative draws on a collection crowded with Huang coverage in many languages. The health narrative is tentative and rests on seven headlines from one day. I have read the Shenzhen declaration as the hinge of the Europe thread for five days, and that framing pulls on how I place each new attack.
line: On 24 November 2026 Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang with Trump's backing, Libya says it will sue Ukraine over Benghazi and US petrol falls most in a month since 2008.
revision: The Iran war thread was revived by judgment after nine editions and its direction reversed from renewed strikes to a contested pause, recorded in withdrawn; the Nvidia thread was resumed after five editions, and a thread on health payments through state channels was begun. The threads on states underwriting data centres and on young protesters fell silent, and the standing was rewritten.
